optional_h3_storyboard_reference.prompt: {{STORYBOARD_REFERENCE}} is the storyboard reference for the mapped shots, defining their viewpoint, framing, subject placement, screen direction, and shot order. Read its visual panels sequentially, one corresponding panel per listed shot, then render exactly one ordinary full-screen moving shot at a time in the requested visual style. The storyboard sheet itself is never visible: no multi-panel grid, split screen, panel borders, divider lines, gutters, white margins, page edges, cropped fragments from adjacent panels, captions, labels, timestamps, or typography.

screenOrientationLock: Viewed-screen orientation lock: whenever a subject reads a phone or detector, the display plane faces that subject's eyes, not the audience. The audience sees the back or edge unless the authored camera is a subject POV or an over-the-shoulder view from behind the subject; in that case the screen remains physically facing the subject while also readable to camera. Hands grip the side or lower edges without covering the viewed content, and wrists remain anatomically plausible.
dialogueTurnPolicy: Exactly one named structured speaker owns each timed line; all other visible humans keep lips closed for that interval.
